record.context_brief: Existence pattern for extremal doubly-even self-dual binary codes
record.original_question: For which positive integers k does there exist a doubly-even self-dual binary code with parameters [24k, 12k, 4k + 4]?

evidence.quote: Open Question 7.7. For which k does there exists a doubly-even self-dual binary [24k, 12k, 4k + 4] code?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length $n$ is a linear subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. Its dual is $C^\perp = \{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n : x\cdot c = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C\}$ with respect to the standard inner product. The code $C$ is self-dual if $C = C^\perp$, and doubly even if the Hamming weight of every codeword is divisible by 4. The minimum distance $d(C)$ is the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. For a doubly even self-dual binary code of length $n = 24k$, the Mallows–Sloane bound gives $d(C) \le 4\lfloor n/24 \rfloor + 4 = 4k+4$; a code attaining this bound is called extremal.

Determine the set of positive integers $k$ for which there exists a doubly even self-dual binary code with parameters $[24k,\,12k,\,4k+4]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. Existence is classically known for $k=1$ (the extended Golay code, $[24,12,8]$) and $k=2$ (the extended quadratic residue code of length 48, $[48,24,12]$). For $k=3$ the existence of a $[72,36,16]$ extremal doubly even self-dual code is a famous long-standing open problem. Non-existence is known for all sufficiently large $k$ (Zhang and subsequent refinements). For most intermediate values of $k$ no extremal code is known nor ruled out.

status_evidence.snippet: Existence of an extremal [72,36,16] doubly even self-dual code is a famous open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The k=3 case of the question is a well-known open problem.

status_evidence.title: On s-extremal singly even self-dual [24k+8,12k+4,4k+2] codes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses non-existence of extremal doubly even self-dual codes of related parameters for k sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Non-existence results are known for sufficiently large k, but the full existence question remains unresolved.
